   constraints and unreliable free-text decisions limit deployment. We present Medotor,
   a locally deployed system for screening patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with
   nasal polyps (CRSwNP) for biologic therapy, and evaluate prompt design on 163
   retrospective cases (132 eligible and 31 ineligible). Five models were tested on the
   same patients under five variants: a minimal prompt (P0), the full
   role/safety/structured nine-point prompt without retrieval (P1), removal of the
   role/safety block (P2), removal of the nine-point schema (P4), and addition to P1 of
   one fixed MemoRAG-derived knowledge block shared by all patients (M0). Every arm
   retained all 163 attempts; undecidable or malformed final decisions were errors.
   Balanced accuracy was the primary metric, with patient-level bootstrap intervals,

   OBJECTIVE: Extract infant breast milk feeding status from electronic health record
   clinical notes to support observational drug-safety studies. MATERIALS AND METHODS:
   Infant notes (19 489; 228 infants) were weakly labeled by large language model (LLM)
   and validated on 1045 manually reviewed notes. Using these labels, we built a rule-
   based medspaCy classifier from a curated feeding term set and compared it with
   ClinPhen and fine-tuned Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers
   (BERT) document classifiers. Maternal postpartum notes (23 mothers; 616 partitions)
   were manually labeled to compare BERT with prompt-based language models. RESULTS: LLM
   labels achieved 99.62% accuracy (macro F1 99.32%). medspaCy achieved 94.36% accuracy
   and 90.40% balanced accuracy (macro F1 0.90) and was applied to 52 278 mother-infant
   dyads. On maternal notes, the prompt-based model improved Positive

6. Feasibility of Privacy-preserving Locally Hosted Language Models for Assessing Medical Student Reflective Writing
Rejeleene R, Byram JN, Frankel RM et al. | Med Sci Educ | 2026-09-01 | relevance 9/10
   https://doi.org/10.1007/s40670-026-02865-7
   Takeaway: [dry-run stub] Takeaway would be generated by the LLM.
   Why: keyword match: llm_evaluation, llm_general_medicine
   UNLABELLED: Reflective writing assessment in medical education is labor-intensive and
   raises data privacy concerns that preclude cloud-based AI solutions. We conducted a
   feasibility study using a locally-hosted, open-weight large language model (LLM)
   deployed on institutional servers to assess medical students' reflective writing. The
   model evaluated 10 de-identified student narratives using two published rubrics
   across three independent passes, generating rubric-aligned scores and formative
   feedback. Scores were consistent across passes and rubrics with no statistically
   significant differences. Expert faculty rated LLM-generated feedback as meeting most
   quality criteria (mean 5.48/7). These findings support feasibility of a privacy-
   preserving, locally-hosted LLM for scalable reflective writing assessment.
   SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material avai
   Feedback: lit feedback +42968798   /   -42968798

   Medical artificial intelligence agents should retrieve patient identifiers only when
   a task requires them, the data-minimization principle behind the HIPAA minimum
   necessary standard for protected health information (PHI). An agent can retrieve
   identifiers without revealing them. Such silent access remains invisible to
   evaluations that inspect only the output. We embedded canaries in synthetic patient
   records and linked each tool invocation to canary exposure in the final answers
   across five language models, four boundary levels, and seven attack frames for
   identifier-free clinical tasks. Three models invoked the PHI tools unnecessarily,
   whereas Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 did not. Stronger boundaries reduced this access,
   and the residual access under the strictest policy was confined to frames in which
   the user overrode the policy or asserted approval. A pre-execution gate given the tas
   Feedback: lit feedback +arxiv:2611.02319   /   -arxiv:2611.02319

Liu J, Liu S | J Med Internet Res | 2026-11-02 | relevance 8/10
   https://doi.org/10.2196/109467
   Takeaway: [dry-run stub] Takeaway would be generated by the LLM.
   Why: keyword match: llm_evaluation
   Clinical AI governance has advanced rapidly in technical validation, regulatory
   compliance, risk management, human oversight, and postdeployment monitoring. Yet a
   more fundamental question often remains implicit: under what conditions are health
   institutions justified in exercising consequential authority through AI over
   patients, clinicians, and communities? In this Viewpoint, we argue that legitimacy
   should be recognized as an independent governance requirement, distinct from
   technical assurance, legal and ethical compliance, trust, acceptance, and
   institutional approval. Our aim is to distinguish institutional approval from public
   authorization and to propose a normative framework for authorizing consequential
   clinical AI deployments. We address health system leaders, clinical AI governance and
   procurement teams, frontline clinicians, and patient and community representatives.

   This multicenter study evaluated early patient-reported outcomes (PROs) among
   individuals initiating twice-yearly lenacapavir (LEN) for HIV preexposure prophylaxis
   (PrEP) in routine care. Convenience, driven by reduced dosing frequency, was the
   primary motivation for LEN initiation, and overall satisfaction was high despite
   frequent but generally mild injection-site reactions. Persistent nodules and pain
   emerged as the leading patient-reported concerns regarding future continuation,
   highlighting the importance of patient-centered counseling and implementation
   strategies to optimize long-term persistence with long-acting PrEP.

   There is an unmet need for repigmentation therapies for patients with nonsegmental
   vitiligo (NSV) who are candidates for systemic therapy. Here, 52-week primary results
   are reported from two parallel phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
   trials of once-daily povorcitinib (oral, highly selective JAK1 inhibitor) 30 mg in
   adults with moderate-to-severe NSV (STOP-V1 and STOP-V2). STOP-V1 and STOP-V2

   ≥75% improvement in the facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (F-VASI75) at week 52 was
   met, demonstrating statistically significant and clinically meaningful repigmentation

   confidence interval 1.6-5.9; P = 0.0003; STOP-V2: 18.9% versus 3.1%; odds ratio, 7.5;

8. Global, regional and national burden of cervical cancer in 1990-2023 with forecasts to 2050: a Global Burden of Disease study
GBD 2023 Cervical Cancer Collaborators | Nat Med | 2026-11-02 | relevance 6/10
   https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-026-04729-4
   Takeaway: [dry-run stub] Takeaway would be generated by the LLM.
   Why: keyword match: major journal
   Although highly preventable, cervical cancer remains one of the most common
   malignancies among women worldwide. As part of the Global Burden of Disease study, we
   estimated cervical cancer incidence, mortality and disability-adjusted life-years
   (DALYs) across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to
   2050. In 2023, 887,000 new cases (95% uncertainty interval 682,000-1,170,000),
   369,000 deaths (292,000-475,000) and 13.3 million DALYs (10.1-17.4) were estimated
   globally. Age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) and age-standardized mortality rates
   (ASMR) were more than four and seven times higher in low- versus high-income
   countries. Between 1990 and 2023, global ASIR was largely stable (-0.4% (-26.6 to
   34.7)), whereas ASMR changed by -17.5% (-36.2 to 13.4). All cervical cancer DALYs
   were attributable to human papillomavirus infection, with tobacco use contributing 5.
